nucleotide flight times through nanoslits can be used for DNA sequencing, but that the nanoslits need to be designed and engineered with the appropriate roughness and patterning to achieve the best possible discrimination.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
molecular dynamics simulation of nucleotide motion through nanochannels can be a useful guide for the design of nanochannels to be used for time of flight based nucleotide sequencing.

molecular dynamics simulations of single DNA nucleotide electrophoretic transport through nanoslits provide a useful tool for optimizing nanoscale devices that might be used to sequence DNA by time-of-flight based methods.
nanochannel design and operation can be used to achieve high-throughput, high-precision, low-cost DNA sequencing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleotide-wall interactions, not ion association, are the main determinants of flight time based nucleotide sequencing.
the nucleotide-wall interactions, rather than ion association, play a dominant role in determining the flight time distributions of single nucleotides through nanochannels and slits.
